closure_proof.line_germ_extension: if a projective line germ lies in Z(F), then F restricted to the full line vanishes as a univariate polynomial
closure_proof.incidence_variety: I={(x,ell): x in ell and ell subset Z(F)} is algebraic because line containment is finitely many coefficient equations
closure_proof.dominance: Monge prolongation gives a line through each generic smooth point, so the projection I -> Z(F) is dominant
closure_proof.grassmannian_image: let Gamma be the Zariski closure of the image of I in G(1,3)
closure_proof.zero_dim_case: dim Gamma=0 cannot dominate an irreducible surface by finitely many lines
closure_proof.one_dim_case: dim Gamma=1 is exactly a one-parameter line family covering a dense open subset
closure_proof.two_dim_case: if dim Gamma>=2, a generic point has a positive-dimensional pencil of contained lines; this forces the tangent plane section to have a plane component, hence the irreducible surface is a plane
closure_proof.conclusion: in every case the irreducible component is ruled

cayley_salmon_transfer.input: F irreducible squarefree, deg(F)<char(k), and Flec(F) vanishes on Z(F)
cayley_salmon_transfer.monge: previous certificate turns the flecnode condition into genuine line germs through generic points
cayley_salmon_transfer.closure: this certificate globalizes those germs through Grassmannian incidence
cayley_salmon_transfer.result: Z(F) is ruled; hence the Cayley-Salmon flecnode criterion is closed in the degree
cayley_salmon_transfer.nonruled_exit: therefore in the non-ruled case Flec(F) is not identically zero on F, so Bezout with deg Flec(F)<=11d gives the O(d^3) line-intersection scale
